lecturer who was instrumental in founding the now defunct
China Study Centre, which was formerly situated at 468 Great

Subject "JEAN HURE", nom de plume used by VICTOR FRENE ( Chinese name:
J. B. Fee ).

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by DBRoss C.D.

On Tuesday, 4th August, I was approached by Mr. G.D. Jack,
with whom I am slightly acquainted, who requested me on behalf
of Mr. Clarke of Clarke's Inquiry Agency, to find out the name
of the person who had written two or three letters to the
Editor of the North China Daily News, under the nom de plume
of "Jean Hure."

I told Mr. Jack that it was impossible to comply with
Mr. Clarke's request but being interested to know why investigat-
ions were being made, I made enquiries and subsequently ascertained
that "Jean Hure" is the pseudonym of Victor Frene (File 3930).

Victor Frene is reported to be a German by birth who has
become a naturalized Chinese and who is now residing at 79 Soochow
Road.

D. P. S.

CHINA'S WOES
Two Evils
1. 8 30
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Enough has been said on the
question whether "Communism and
Japanese Imperialism" is a greater
curse to China than "Personal Mili-
tarism." I shall desist, and would
apologize for usurping so much of your
valuable space on a purely domestic
question which may not be of in-
terest to your foreign readers. The
fact is both the two evils are curses
of China and it does not matter
much which is the greater curse.
With the elimination of Chen Chi-
tang and his associates from Liang
Kwang "Personal Militarism" is
nearly passed.
I must apologise for speaking of
the Generalissimo's rather than of the
Government's generosity as F.D.Z. has
so kindly called my attention. Indeed
have I erred. The reason I have
made the mistake is because, as the
President of the Executive Yuan, the
Generalissimo, is the actual head of
the National Government, in ac-
cordance with the Organic Law. I
had in mind this official capacity
when I wrote of the Generalissimo's
generosity to his antagonists.
It is difficult to understand why
should both this time and F.D.Z.
worry about the question of Gen-
eral Pai's service when at the time
of their writing, the appointment of
General Pai to the post of Governor-
ship of Chekiang has already been
gazetted. The question is not wheth-
er the Government want his ser-
vice but whether he wishes to serve
or not.
No matter how gifted an officer
and administrator, General Pai may
be, his present defection has in fact
disqualified him for any position of
confidence with the Government.
How are we sure that we can depend
upon him in an emergency? To
divest him of the command of the
army that might place its allegiance
to him personally, above that to the
nation, is justifiable and proper.
These words are sincerely intended in
the nation's interest. There is no
room in the army for a player who
persists in playing to the grand
stand. General Pai, the star player
must take warning, learn to obey the
captain, and play his duly assigned
position like the rest, like a good
sport. On the other hand if his per-
sonal ambition and alignment
prevent his working in perfect har-
mony with the National Government
it would be advisable for him to "follow
the example of Marshal Chang Chi-
tsao" as suggested in your recent
leader entitled "Liberation."
In conclusion, I wish to express my
deep appreciation for the several
articles which recently appeared in
your esteemed journal in connection
with the subject of Personal Milita-
rism. They have done much to clar-
ify the situation and to bring home
to the public the urgent need for
national unity and solidarity. I am
convinced that only through such
unity can China hope to overcome
the many difficulties that confront
her today.
For attention
A. S. Hutchins

中国的苦难
两大弊病
1. 8 30

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——关于“共产主义和日本帝国主义”是否比“个人军事独裁”对中国危害更大的问题，已经说得够多了。我将就此打住，并为在一个纯粹的内政问题上占用贵报宝贵篇幅而道歉，这可能不会引起您的外国读者的兴趣。事实是，这两大弊病都是中国的祸害，哪一个危害更大并不重要。

随着陈济棠及其同伙在两广地区的被清除，“个人军事独裁”几乎已成为过去。

我必须为提及委员长而非政府的慷慨而道歉，正如 F.D.Z. 好意提醒我的那样。确实是我错了。我犯这个错误的原因是，根据《组织法》，作为行政院院长的委员长是国民政府的实际首脑。我在写到委员长对其对手的慷慨时，心中所想的是他的这一官方身份。

难以理解为何这次和 F.D.Z. 都要为白将军的服务问题而担忧，因为在他们写信时，任命白将军为浙江省主席的公告已经发布。问题不在于政府是否需要他的服务，而在于他是否愿意服务。

无论白将军作为一名军官和管理者多么有天赋，他目前的叛离行为实际上已使他失去担任政府任何信任职位的资格。我们如何确信在紧急情况下可以依赖他？剥夺他对军队的指挥权是正当且合适的，因为这可能使军队对他的个人效忠高于对国家的效忠。这些话是真诚地为了国家利益而说的。军队中没有容身之处给那些坚持为了博取眼球而表演的人。明星球员白将军必须吸取教训，学会服从队长，并像其他队员一样，像个好的运动员那样打好分配给他的位置。另一方面，如果他的个人野心和立场阻碍他与国民政府完美和谐地工作，那么他最好“效仿张作霖元帅”，正如贵报近期题为《解放》的社论中所建议的那样。

最后，我想对贵刊最近发表的几篇关于个人军事独裁主题的文章表示深深的感谢。这些文章极大地澄清了局势，并使公众认识到国家统一和团结的迫切需求。我深信，只有通过这样的团结，中国才有希望克服今天面临的许多困难。

供注意
A. S. Hutchins

Hint to Nanking

To the Editor of the
"North-China Daily News"

Sir,—Because Mr. Kao Kwok, in his letter of July 31, published in your issue of August 1, under the title of "Two Evils" still mentions my name, I hope you will allow me to say a few words in reply to him. I am glad to be able to quote part of your leading article of July 31 entitled, "Question of Method" in refutation of Mr. Kao Kwok's argument, in the expectation that Mr. Kao Kwok may in this way, be more easily induced to pay attention to certain points, which he seems to have overlooked.

You write:

The Central Government is aware that in such matters pure logic is an unreliable guide. One of the most attractive, yet often embarrassing traits of Chinese thought, is the belief in the methods of compromise. The defeated enemy is seldom pressed to extremes. The unsuccessful litigant is often given more than he deserves lest the disgrace of failure should unduly depress him and so discomfort the court. It was felt that the original decision to confirm the Kwangsi generals in their present posts had something of that spirit. Now it is pointed out that the confirmation was agreed upon when Kwangtung was still defiant. Its reversal by deciding on the transfer of the two officers—other important—but in most men's eyes less significant—posts, is being criticized by a strong section of opinion which in other respects supports the National Government Friends of Nanking, in fact, fear lest the Government should be rushed into an error which might mar the exceedingly good impression made by its general handling of a difficult situation.

Towards the end of your leader, you say:

If the two generals could give definite assurance that their conduct at Kwangsi would be in the future would strictly conform to the requirements of the Central Government, especially in the national interest, and could produce some guarantees of acceptable character, the Central Government might conceivably be able to review the position. This point is worth considering, for a conciliatory attitude will doubtless avert any risk of their actions being interpreted as dictated by personal pique or desire of revenge. They are not without influence in the Kwangsi army and their co-operation would greatly facilitate the task of restoring order and tranquillity in that province. It is therefore desirable that every effort should be made to secure their willing acquiescence in the new arrangement.

中国的困境
给南京的暗示

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，由于高国（Kao Kwok，音译）先生在7月31日致贵报、并于8月1日刊出、题为“两种弊端”的信中仍然提及我的名字，我希望您能允许我略陈数语以作答复。我很高兴能引用贵报7月31日题为“方法问题”的社论的一部分，来驳斥高国先生的论点，期望通过这种方式，能更容易地促使高国先生注意某些他似乎已经忽略的要点。

阁下写道：

中央政府意识到，在此类事务中，纯粹的逻辑并不可靠。中国思想中最具吸引力、却又常令人尴尬的特征之一，便是对妥协方法的信奉。对于被击败的敌人，很少会被逼至绝境。败诉的一方往往得到的多于其应得之物，以免失败的耻辱使其过度沮丧，从而令法庭感到不安。人们认为，最初决定确认广西将领现任原职的决定，便带有这种精神。现在有人指出，这项确认是在广东方面仍然持对抗态度时达成的。如今决定调动这两名军官——其他重要、但在大多数人眼中较不显著的——职位，从而推翻之前的决定，正受到一部分舆论的批评，而这部分舆论在其他方面是支持国民政府的。事实上，南京之友担心政府会仓促行事而犯下错误，这可能损害其在总体处理这一困难局面时所留下的极佳印象。

在社论末尾，阁下说道：

如果这两位将军能够明确保证，他们今后在广西的行为将严格遵守中央政府的要求，特别是符合国家利益，并能提出某种性质可接受的担保，那么中央政府或许有可能重新审视这一局势。这一点值得考虑，因为和解的态度无疑将避免任何将其行动解读为出于个人怨愤或报复欲望的风险。他们在广西军队中并非没有影响力，他们的合作将极大地促进恢复该省秩序与安宁的任务。因此，宜尽一切努力争取他们自愿默许新的安排。

先生，——如果上海的外侨社群对中国政治能多几分关注，那么贵报8月4日题为《孤注一掷之举》的社论必将赢得一片喝彩。该社论第二段的首句以科学术语揭示了广西危机的心理根源。阁下写道：“如今有一种观点颇受尊重，即侵略行为可能源于对合法成长或自然行动自由受到限制的理性或非理性恐惧。”所有了解李宗仁将军的人都知道，迫使他努力通过抵抗外来干涉以确保广西进展安全的，确实无非是“对合法成长及自然行动自由受到限制的恐惧”。贵报社论提及“两位广西将军为国民党事业及其所辖省份作出的卓越贡献”。阁下还补充说，“没有任何一个省份能比广西更好地贯彻蒋介石将军关于通过密切关注农民需求来击败共产主义宣传的主张。”阁下建议“应尽一切可能在不诉诸武力的情况下平息局势”，并得出结论认为，“如果蒋介石将军能够赢得”广西将领的合作，“他将取得其职业生涯中最引人注目的政治胜利”。阁下对这场现代中国悲剧中主要角色动机的理解足够深刻，足以促使阁下告知他们，“鉴于中央政府 prevailing 的新精神，他们对于成为牺牲品的担忧已经过时。”

南京政府拥有白崇禧将军这样一位一流的创造性合作者。可以预期，近十年的政务管理经验已使蒋介石将军认识到，创造性合作作为促进其宏大计划成功的手段，其价值所在。作为一名熟读经典的学生，蒋将军会记得那句经典名言：

“独木难支。但若合力，则如山之广大；两理可协同；三山合一；从而万事……”

CHINESE BEHAVIOUR
IS EXPLAINED
Dr. Victor Frene Gives
An Analysis Of The
Vital Difference

“Why does a Chinese behave as
he does?” This is a question which
many foreign residents of Shang-
hai ask themselves every day. But
most of them, very quickly, give
up the attempt of ever finding a
reply. And perhaps no other race
is more difficult to explain than
the Chinese. Supported by 20
years of experience gained in a
purely Chinese environment and by
years of scientifically psychological
training, Dr. Victor Frene, yester-
day, in a lecture given at the
Foreign Y.M.C.A., attempted to
give an outline of a scientific
analysis of Chinese behaviour.
The lecture was divided into two
parts: 1.—The Chinese type of
behaviourism. 2.—The strong and
weak points of Chinese behaviour-
ism. In essence, Dr. Frene
suggested that, whilst human
behaviour, in Western behaviour-
ish, is conceived as the outcome
of the interaction between the
stimulation produced by the
environment and the reaction
generated by the human body, in
Chinese behaviour it was the brain
which provided the stimulus and
the body which provided the reac-
tion. According to Dr. Frene,
Chinese behaviour was, therefore,
indeed the exact reversal of
Occidental behaviour. That was
what rendered Chinese behaviour
so incomprehensible to non-Chinese.
Chinese behaviourism was, accord-
ing to Dr. Frene, the first step
towards a scientific analysis of
the Chinese mind.

维克多·弗伦博士分析
关键差异

“为什么中国人的行为如此？”这是许多上海外侨每天自问的问题。但大多数人很快就放弃了寻找答案的尝试。也许没有哪个民族比中国人更难解释了。凭借在纯中文环境中获得的20年经验以及多年的科学心理学训练，维克多·弗伦博士昨天在外侨青年会举行的讲座中，试图勾勒出对中国人行为进行科学分析的轮廓。
讲座分为两部分：1. 中国人的行为主义类型。2. 中国人行为主义的优缺点。本质上，弗伦博士指出，虽然西方行为主义将人类行为视为环境产生的刺激与人体产生的反应之间相互作用的结果，但在中国人的行为中，是大脑提供刺激，身体提供反应。据弗伦博士称，因此，中国人的行为确实是西方行为的完全反转。这正是使中国人的行为对非华人来说如此难以理解的原因。据弗伦博士称，中国人行为主义是科学分析中国人心智的第一步。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 17, 1933

FROM CHINESE ART
TO LABOUR

Discussions in Four Lectures
by Dr. V. Frass

From psychology through literature, music and painting down to the question of efficiency of manual labour and to that of the efficiency of productive power and mental power, that was the road along which Dr. Victor Frass has guided his hearers in the course of the four lectures on Chinese problems which constituted the first series of his lectures given before the China Study Centre.

The last of the four lectures was entitled “Hill-Water-Pictures”. This lecture was given on Monday afternoon and was divided into three parts: 1. What Painting means in China. 2. The Comparative Value of Chinese Paintings. 3. Elements of the Psychology of “Hill-Water” Pictures. The lecture was brought to conclusion with a discussion of the question of China’s mental efficiency.

In this lecture, Dr. Frass demonstrated the fact that Chinese painting, in its essence, was not a reproduction of objects but meant to bring out what, in modern terminology, would be called a collection of symbols, descriptive of nature and the movements of the human mind. He pointed out that these are the only kind of Chinese paintings to be considered as truly representative of Chinese art, and that all other kinds of Chinese painting, such as portraits, flower-and-bird pictures, etc., are of secondary importance. He further explained that the “Hill-Water” pictures are not merely representations of natural scenery, but are expressions of the artist’s inner world, reflecting his philosophical and spiritual outlook. The lecture concluded with a discussion on how these artistic principles relate to the broader question of China’s mental efficiency and its impact on labour and productivity.

从中国艺术到劳工

V. 弗拉斯博士（Dr. V. Frass，音译）的四场讲座讨论

从心理学经过文学、音乐和绘画，直到体力劳动效率问题以及生产力和智力效率问题，这是维克多·弗拉斯博士在构成其在中国学社发表的第一系列讲座的四场关于中国问题的讲座中引导听众走过的道路。

四场讲座中的最后一场题为“山水画”。这场讲座于周一下午举行，分为三个部分：1. 绘画在中国的意义。2. 中国绘画的比较价值。3. “山水”画的心理学要素。讲座以讨论中国智力效率问题告终。

在这场讲座中，弗拉斯博士论证了一个事实，即中国绘画的本质不是物体的再现，而是意在展现用现代术语称为的描述自然和人类心智运动的符号集合。他指出，只有这类中国绘画才被视为真正代表中国艺术，而其他种类的中国绘画，如肖像画、花鸟画等，则处于次要地位。他进一步解释说，“山水”画不仅仅是自然景色的表现，而是艺术家内心世界的表达，反映了他的哲学和精神观。讲座最后讨论了这些艺术原则如何与中国智力效率这一更广泛的问题及其对劳动和生产力的影响相关联。

Sketch of a
Lecture given on September 25th, 1933,
at THE CHINA STUDY CENTER
by

------------------

NOT FOR PUBLICATION.          ALL RIGHTS RESERVED.

Today's lecture is meant as an introduction
to the psychological group of studies and I intend to give
other lectures as introductions into all the other groups.
Next Monday I intend to give a sketch of the most important
ideas contained in the Chinese Classics, and on Monday,
October 9th, a lecture on Chinese music; on the 16th, a
lecture on Chinese Painting. These four lectures will be
most intimately connected because the lecture on Chinese
Classics will prove the essential statements contained in
today's lecture, and the lectures on Chinese music and
Painting will aid other proofs. Naturally, all these four
lectures cannot be complete in all details - they are only
sketches - and today's lecture is bound to be the most
sketchy of the four. Today's lecture is bound to be the
most sketchy of the four, because today's lecture is
naturally the most complicated. But I ask you kindly not
to be impatient and to let me know of the objections and
doubts and questions you may have, because our way of
discussing things is entirely new and therefore there are
bound to be many doubts and many, many, questions. I shall
do my best to solve these doubts and to find answers to the
questions.

Today's subject is "THE PSYCHOLOGICAL
DISCOVERY OF CHINA". Before I begin my discussion I have
to point out that what I mean by "psychology" is something
very, very, different from what is ordinarily understood
by psychology. Today the term "psychology" is still open
to so much misinterpretation that I have first to explain
what I do not mean by it. To that purpose, I shall quote
George A. Dorsey, the American authority, who has very
admirably described what psychology has meant up to now.

"Of all the theories I studied in school, the
one that gave me the least light on man and myself was
psychology -- accounting, possibly, mineralogy. It worried
me. I wanted to learn about my own and man's psyche, and if
not, I assumed it was because the course was over my head.
It was. For this reason. To the old psychology heads
were like crystals - by gazing into them, called 'introspection'
the mind could be seen and studied. Crystal-gazing never
did call itself a science; mind gazing did; but is now also
only a cult. The introspectors could not agree as to what
they saw. But that they were looking at 'mind' they had no
doubt. Their logic was simple and convincing; mind is not
matter - the body is matter; mind and body, therefore are

维克多·弗雷尔（Victor Frere）博士

所作讲座之概要

不得发表。          版权所有。

今天的讲座旨在作为心理学研究小组的入门介绍，我打算为所有其他研究小组也提供类似的入门讲座。下周一，我打算概要介绍中国经典中所包含的最重要思想；10月9日星期一，将举办关于中国音乐的讲座；16日，将举办关于中国绘画的讲座。这四次讲座将紧密相连，因为关于中国经典的讲座将证明今天讲座中所包含的基本论点，而关于中国音乐和绘画的讲座则将辅助提供其他证据。当然，所有这四场讲座在细节上都不可能面面俱到——它们只是概要——而今天的讲座必然是四场中最为简略的。今天的讲座必然是四场中最为简略的，因为今天的讲座自然是最为复杂的。但我恳请诸位不要不耐烦，并请将你们可能有的反对意见、疑虑和问题告知我，因为我们讨论事物的方式完全是全新的，因此必然会有许多疑虑和许许多多问题。我将尽力消除这些疑虑并找到问题的答案。

今天的主题是“中国的心理发现”。在开始讨论之前，我必须指出，我所指的“心理学”与通常所理解的心理学有着非常、非常不同的含义。如今，“心理学”一词仍极易被误解，因此我首先必须解释我不指代的是什么。为此，我将引用美国权威人士乔治·A·多尔西（George A. Dorsey）的话，他对迄今为止心理学的含义作了极为精彩的描述。

“在我于学校研习的所有理论中，给予我和他人性最少启发的便是心理学——或许还有会计学、矿物学。它令我困扰。我想了解我自己以及人类的 psyche（心灵/精神），若未能如愿，我便假定是因为课程超出了我的理解能力。确实如此。原因在于。对于旧派心理学家而言，头脑如同水晶——通过凝视它们，即所谓‘内省’，便可观察和研究心智。水晶占卜从未自称为科学；心智凝视却自称科学；但如今它也仅仅是一种崇拜流派。内省者们对他们所见之物无法达成一致。但他们毫无疑问自己正在审视‘心智’。他们的逻辑简单而令人信服：心智非物质——身体是物质；因此，心智与身体是

separate and distinct entities. They turned the body over to
sawbones and kept 'mind' for themselves and went on arguing
about what they saw in it.

'I see red,' says one. 'Is it pure?' asks another.
'Is it perception, sensation, connotation, or ideation; or
is it a conception, or the imagination? Is it as content,
awareness, or as ego? If as ego, can you time it; if as
awareness, can you weigh it?'. This is all nonsense, of
course, but not more so than the psychology I studied in
school".

That is what Dorsey says and I am very glad to

us as far as I can see is that this traditional psychology
has up to now never been of any use to those who wanted to
understand themselves. Up to now psychology has not become
a science and has therefore fulfilled none of the functions
of science. If psychology had already become a science and
been used as a science we all would be able to manage our

of the fundamental doctrine of scientific morality - dynamic

我们可以这样总结对中国心理学这门科学的简要描述：在中国人的生活中，除了那些与心灵最接近的感官外，所有其他感官都被认为毫无重要性。因此，中国文明从未发明过浴缸，也不懂卫生，同样不懂道路修筑。看看这扇大门外的道路——那是一条中国市政道路。它们都是那个样子。即使是使用了一年的机动车道看起来也是那样——它们在退化——回归到原始状态。他们的文明仅由文学、音乐和绘画构成。人类所创造的最崇高的文学是中国的。最崇高的音乐心理学也是中国的，而真正的绘画、艺术性的绘画、心理上健康的绘画，唯在中国可见。

这三者是从最高级的感觉器官演化而来的；这是在中国被允许发挥功能的唯一感觉器官。言语——耳和眼。言语感、听觉感和视觉感，由此我进入第二章：-

二、 中国心理结构的表现。

这种将大脑作为生命驱动力、并努力使大脑尽可能保持其原始状态（这意味着尽可能少地刺激它，或尽可能温柔地，或尽可能微妙地刺激它）的中国原生倾向，引导真正的中国人通过构建一种可称为纯粹审美性的文明来表达自己。它拒绝承认生活的事实，掩盖丑陋，并试图规避那些无法改变的物理事实。由于这种中国审美文明的驱动力是一种并非源自感官力量的脑力，因此中国人的所思与所做之间经常存在公开的矛盾。许多人注意到，中国人倾向于宣扬最崇高的原则和思想，却未能将其付诸实践；或者即使付诸实践，也做得如此糟糕，以至于原始理念几乎荡然无存。这在心理上或许可以解释为：中国文明建立在这样一种特定的脑力之上，而这种脑力并非源自感官力量。

中国的这种特定脑力导致了其他同样令人惊讶、且往往令外国观察者反感的表现。

我将仅再引用一个此类表现的例子。

在日常生活中，你经常注意到一种看似说谎的倾向。许多外国人觉得这种倾向令人恼火。但我们相信，心理学将教导在华的外国人：中国人并不是真的在说谎；他只是说出他所相信的；说出他期望成为的样子；说出他内心希望成为的样子。在这方面他像个孩子——像孩子一样，他从不撒谎。像孩子一样，他虚构

who condemn the Chinese because they are lying are just
as wrong as the mothers who punish their children because
they are lying.

Foreign judges of China, as well as this kind of
mother, prove that they have never carefully studied the
psychology of the people with whom they are dealing.
Their failure to study their psychology, is, of course,
not their own fault, but only that of our schools, who
either do not teach psychology at all or teach it in the
absurd fashion described by Dorsey.

The relation of what is usually believed to be
lying leads us immediately to that of the function of the
ore sense organ of the human body which is most intimately
connected with brain. This sense organ is speech.

Speech is the highest sense organ - only human beings
have speech because only the human being has a fully
developed brain. It is what science teaches. Speech is
a transformation of all kinds of sense impressions. What I
see, is transformed in speech, into a sound. What I touch,
is transformed by speech into sound. Speech is produced
when all the impressions we receive by our senses have
passed through the brain and have been transformed into
sound. So nothing on earth is closer to brain than speech
and all the great thinkers and teachers are great talkers
and all the mentally active nations have a very rich
literature. Therefore all the Oriental nations have
tremendous treasures of literature. In China even the
ricksha coolies talk and talk. If they can read a little
they will do their best to make use of the light they
obtain in the street while waiting for a fare, in order
to do a little reading. They buy those little books
for one or two coppers and they read them in spite of all.
All the ricksha men like to talk, all the amahs like to
talk, every farmer is delighted when he can talk.

They are not afraid of the Japanese as long as they
can make walls, walls. As long as they can say "Down
with Imperialism" they are convinced that Imperialism
is on the way to breaking down and when they say "Down with
consular jurisdiction" or "Give us back the concessions",
they believe that they have nothing else to do to abolish
consular jurisdiction to get the concessions back.
It is the greatest pleasure of the Chinese to talk and they
are firmly convinced that by talking about things they really
get them done. A nation which lives on brain energy more
than on energy derived from muscles any other organ contained
in the body is bound to be a nation which worships the sense
of speech.

To come back to my own experience. During the last
20 years I have had the greatest success in so far as the
talking was concerned, but I have had no success at all in
my attempts at seeing my plans realised in practice. I
have found it nearly impossible to get things done in the
way they should be done and found it equally impossible to
make people realise that everything has its law in itself
and that arbitrary alterations to projects destroy the
possibility of their realization. I have found it very

对中国的外国评判者，以及这类母亲，都证明他们从未仔细研究过他们所打交道的人群的心理。他们未能研究其心理，当然不是他们自己的过错，而只是我们学校的过错，这些学校要么根本不教授心理学，要么以多尔西（Dorsey）所描述的那种荒谬方式教授心理学。

通常被认为是说谎的行为，直接引导我们去关注与大脑联系最紧密的人体主要感觉器官的功能。这个感觉器官就是言语。

言语是最高级的感觉器官——只有人类拥有言语，因为只有人类拥有完全发育的大脑。这是科学所教导的。言语是各种感官印象的转化。我所看到的，在言语中被转化为声音。我所触摸的，通过言语被转化为声音。当我们通过感官接收到的所有印象经过大脑并被转化为声音时，言语便产生了。因此，世上没有任何事物比言语更接近大脑，所有伟大的思想家和教师都是健谈者，所有精神活跃的民族都拥有丰富的文学。因此，所有东方民族都拥有巨大的文学宝藏。在中国，甚至连黄包车夫都在不停地交谈。如果他们识一点字，他们会尽力利用在街头等待客人时获得的一点光亮，进行少许阅读。他们花一两枚铜板购买那些小册子，并且不顾一切地阅读。所有的黄包车夫都喜欢交谈，所有的阿妈（amahs）都喜欢交谈，每个农民在能够交谈时都会感到高兴。

只要他们能筑起墙壁，墙壁，他们就不怕日本人。只要他们能说“打倒帝国主义”，他们就确信帝国主义正在走向崩溃；而当他们说“废除领事裁判权”或“归还租界”时，他们相信无需再做其他事情就能废除领事裁判权并收回租界。交谈是中国人最大的乐趣，他们坚信通过谈论事情就能真正把事情做成。一个依靠脑力而非依靠肌肉或身体内其他器官产生的能量生活的民族，注定是一个崇拜言语感的民族。

回到我个人的经历。在过去20年里，我在言谈方面取得了最大的成功，但在试图将我的计划付诸实践方面却毫无成功。我发现几乎不可能以应有的方式把事情做成，也同样不可能让人们认识到每件事物都有其内在规律，而对项目的任意更改会破坏其实现的可能性。我发现非常

easy to make people say "You are right". I am discovering
more and more that it was a mistake to expect the Chinese
to do the thing which they acknowledge to be right.

Thinking and doing are contradictions in China.
There is no connection between the two. The great
revolutionary leader Dr. Sun Yat sen has revealed this
fundamental weakness of China and therefore postulated that
psychological reconstruction would have to precede material
reconstruction in China. But this postulate has, up to now,
remained a pious wish and neither Dr. Sun Yat Sen nor any
of his successors have ever endeavoured to change this
fundamental trait of Chinese psychology and to build a bridge
between thinking and doing. It goes without saying that
the building of such a bridge would be a psychological
task of very first magnitude and that there was up to now
no psychology available for such an undertaking.

There is another Chinese leader who has also discovered
the existence of the gap between thinking and doing in China.
This leader is the famous Dr. Hu Shih. Dr. Hu Shih has
pointed out that there exists in China a kind of religion,
which he calls "The religion of names". He would like to call
it a superstitious belief in the supreme power of speech.
This superstition causes the Chinese to take delight in the
invention of slogans of the kind mentioned above and to believe
that a new slogan means a step forward on the road of progress.
It should be understood also that Dr. Hu Shih who has analysed
the essential psychological trait of China with so much clear
sight, has, as far as I know, never made the slightest effort
to discover a cure for this psychological disease.

To continue with our study of the manifestation of
the psychological constitution of China, we have to say that
the second comparatively important sense organ in China is the
ear. It is the ear which provides the technical means for
the invention of speech. But the ear leads not only to the
invention of speech and literature but also to that of the
second great art of China. This second great art is music.
What I shall endeavour to provide in this lecture on the
Psychology of Chinese music will be based upon the outcome
of the research which I made more than 20 years ago in
Paris and London. At that time I published a great number
of booklets on Oriental music as a whole, not only in Paris
and London, but also in Italy. I shall be very glad to have
the opportunity of taking up again in the forthcoming lecture
on music my former studies from a new point of view and I hope
that the lecture on music will prove to be most useful for the
discussion of problems most intimately connected with today's
lecture.

Also the manifestation of the third most important sense
organ of China, which is the eye, I shall postpone to another
day. On that day, in watching the function of the eye in
China we shall analyse Chinese painting. This discussion on
Chinese painting will be very closely related to that on
Chinese music.

Today in concluding the second chapter I invite you to
remember that in my contention the three senses - of speech,
hearing and the sense of sight, are the only three which are
used as a means of manifesting the psychological constitution
of China.

在中国，思与行是矛盾的。两者之间没有联系。伟大的革命领袖孙中山博士揭示了中国这一根本弱点，因此提出在中国心理重建必须先于物质重建。但这一主张迄今为止仍只是一个美好的愿望，无论是孙中山博士还是他的任何继任者，都从未努力改变中国心理的这一根本特征，并在思与行之间架起桥梁。不言而喻，架设这样一座桥梁将是头等重要的心理任务，而迄今为止，尚无适用于此类事业的心理学可用。

还有另一位中国领导人也发现了中国思与行之间存在鸿沟。这位领导人就是著名的胡适博士。胡适博士指出，中国存在一种他称之为“名教”的宗教。他愿意将其称为对言语至高权力的迷信信仰。这种迷信使中国人乐于发明上述这类口号，并相信一个新口号就意味着在进步道路上迈出了一步。还应当理解的是，胡适博士虽然以如此清晰的眼光分析了中国基本的心理特征，但据我所知，他从未做出丝毫努力去寻找治愈这种心理疾病的良方。

继续我们要对中国心理结构表现的研究，我们必须说，在中国，第二个相对重要的感觉器官是耳朵。耳朵为言语的发明提供了技术手段。但耳朵不仅导致言语和文学的发明，也导致中国第二大门类艺术的产生。这第二大门类艺术就是音乐。我在本次关于中国音乐心理学的讲座中将要提供的内容，将基于我二十多年前在巴黎和伦敦进行的研究成果。当时，我在巴黎、伦敦以及意大利出版了大量关于东方音乐整体的小册子。我将非常高兴有机会在即将举行的音乐讲座中，从新的角度重新探讨我以前的研究，并希望这次音乐讲座能证明对讨论与今天讲座最密切相关的问题极为有用。

至于中国第三大重要感觉器官——眼睛的表现，我也将推迟到另一天再讲。在那一天，通过观察眼睛在中国的功能，我们将分析中国绘画。关于中国绘画的讨论将与关于中国音乐的讨论密切相关。

今天在结束第二章时，我请各位记住，依我的观点，言语、听觉和视觉这三种感官，是唯一被用作表现中国心理结构手段的三种感官。

iii. THE ILL-EFFECTS OF THIS PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTITUTION OF CH...

Some of these ill-effects we have already mentioned in
the second chapter; but those which we shall discuss in this
chapter are unmixed evils while those mentioned in the second c...
were, to a certain extent, only what the French call "accidents
de travail". The effects mentioned in the third chapter, because
they are unmixed evils, will be very easily realised by you who
are living in China and have experience of Chinese life.

In consequence of the habit of using only the highest
senses, i.e. those senses which were most closely connected with
the brain, all the lower senses were thrown out of employment,
not only during two or three years of depression, but out of
employment for 5,000 or 10,000 years.

We shall first briefly mention that also the highest
senses in real China were only partly put to use by Chinese
psychology, for instance, the sense of sight only in so far as
it transforms things most completely, was allowed to function.
But to have the sense of sight functioning as an organ unmixt
for convincing, was considered as degradation. To copy things as
they are then, to produce an art which would be something like
artistic photography, was absolutely undesirable and strictly
forbidden by Chinese moral psychology. Also the ear was allowed
to listen to long sounds, which had no clearly defined rhythm
whatever. I shall, in my lecture on music, endeavour to let
you hear as far as possible what these sounds were like. But
anything like dance music, or like our jazz, was undesirable
to the real Chinese.

As far as literature is concerned, stories like most
of our novels, plays like our film-farces, all these kinds of
literature were entirely below the level of the real literature
of China.

These three examples show that also the highest senses
in China were allowed to function freely only in so far as their
highest activities were concerned.

But the lower senses, for instances the sense of touch
the sense of sex, which is the strongest of the senses based upon
touch and skin, were crushed out of existence by Chinese
psychology. Sex is a combination of all the senses of the human
body and therefore the most powerful of all senses. The more
powerful the sense is, the more dangerous it was from the point
of view of the real Chinese psychology which did its best to
protect the brain against sense stimulation, and to preserve
the original quietude of the mind. This is the real reason which
underlies the Chinese habit of teaching young people that their
parents must choose their wives or husbands. The young man in
China gets married without asking questions. In many cases
when a Chinese sees his wife for the first time, he is horrified,
but this feeling of horror does not prevent him from marrying and
from having children. "Askee, raskee, getting married, not a
very important matter for a moral man". Sex is outside of his
sphere of serious thought. "Why worry about such things." "Jeje
fatze" say the Chinese.

I should very much welcome a new Miss Mayo who would
write a book on Mother China as she has written one on Mother
India. The study of the influence of this attitude towards sex
on the race and civilization of China would demand very careful
research, and would require a specialist.

iii. 中国这种心理结构的不良后果...

我们在第二章中已经提到了其中一些不良后果；但本章要讨论的那些是纯粹的危害，而第二章中提到的那些在某种程度上只是法国人所谓的“工伤事故”。第三章中提到的影响，因为它们是纯粹的危害，对于生活在中国并有中国生活经验的你们来说，将很容易理解。

由于只使用最高级感官（即与大脑联系最紧密的那些感官）的习惯，所有低级感官不仅在这两三年的萧条期间被闲置，而且在五千或一万年间都被闲置。

我们首先要简要提及，即使在真正的中国，最高级感官也只是被中国心理学部分地加以利用，例如，视觉仅在其能最彻底地转化事物的范围内才被允许发挥作用。但是，让视觉作为一种纯粹的说服器官来发挥作用，则被视为堕落。因此，如实摹写事物，创作一种类似艺术摄影的艺术，是绝对不受欢迎的，并且受到中国道德心理学的严格禁止。同样，耳朵也只被允许聆听那些没有任何明确节奏的长音。我将在我的音乐讲座中，尽可能让你们听到这些声音是什么样子的。但对于真正的中国人来说，任何类似舞曲或类似我们的爵士乐的东西都是不受欢迎的。

就文学而言，像我们大多数小说那样的故事，像我们的滑稽电影那样的戏剧，所有这些类型的文学都完全低于中国真正文学的水平。

这三个例子表明，在中国，最高级感官也仅在其最高级活动方面被允许自由发挥作用。

但是，低级感官，例如触觉，以及基于触觉和皮肤的最强烈的感官——性觉，被中国心理学压制至不复存在。性是人类身体所有感官的结合，因此是所有感官中最强大的。感官越强大，从真正的中国心理学角度来看就越危险，因为中国心理学尽力保护大脑免受感官刺激，并保持心灵原本的宁静。这正是中国人习惯教导年轻人必须由父母为其选择妻子或丈夫的根本原因。中国的年轻人在结婚时不问任何问题。在许多情况下，当中国男子第一次见到他的妻子时，他会感到惊恐，但这种惊恐感并不妨碍他结婚生子。“问也不问，娶了就娶，对于一个有道德的人来说，这不是什么大事”。性不在他严肃思考的范畴之内。“何必为这种事烦恼。”中国人说“济济法子”（音译）。

我非常欢迎出现一位新的梅奥小姐（Miss Mayo），她能像撰写《印度母亲》那样撰写一本关于《中国母亲》的书。研究这种对性的态度对中国种族和文明的影响，需要非常仔细的研究，也需要专家来进行。

The absolute incapacity of appreciating the value of
sex, meant naturally incapacity of producing any of the different
forms of what we call love, because all forms of love including
friendship between man and man, and woman and woman, are
sublimations of sex, and all human relations are evolved out
of sex. All nations which fail to sublimate sex, do not get
to know what love is, and do not obtain the opportunity of
exploiting any of the different forms of love many of which
are so tremendously important as driving forces for the
upbuilding of human society. Any so-called experts on China
believe that when they point out that there is no real feeling
of cohesion between the Chinese, no capacity of collaboration
and organization, they have discovered one of the most serious
defects of Chinese civilization, but psychology teaches that
the root of this Chinese incapacity of collaboration and
organization is to be found at the point which most of these
experts never take into consideration. This point is the one
which I have reached just now in pointing out that the
incapacity of collaboration and organization is nothing but an
outcome of the incapacity of bringing about the general feeling
of human sympathy, which would be another form of sublimation
of sex. I am here today making use of the example of neglect
of sex to enable you to understand how disastrous the neglect
of the development of the lower senses was in China.

I have one thing to add here which I believe to be very
important. This Chinese attitude of considering all the lower
senses to be of no importance, was intentionally and carefully
developed, because, in weakening the lower senses, the brain
was cut off from connection with all those kinds of stimulation
which were considered as most dangerous in real China, the
stimulations coming from nature. The ancient Chinese taught
that the fundamental sin was abandoning oneself to matter,
to nature; what we would call in one word, objectivity. This
danger of committing a sin, a mortal sin, was avoided
intentionally, avoided by killing all the lower senses, and
this killing of the lower senses became a means of rendering
the abandonment of the individual to anything like purely
physical stimulation impossible. This Chinese tendency of
killing the lower senses is therefore just as essential to
Chinese psychology as it is dangerous for the maintenance
of life power and of power of action in Chinese civilization.

We may add more facts which demonstrate the disastrous
effect of this Chinese habit of neglecting the lower senses.
Here skin is considered unimportant, people do not feel dirt,
dust or uncleanliness of any kind. The neglect of the sense
of touch leads not only to neglect of cleanliness but
produces also the incapacity of keeping things in repair.
Because of his lack of perceiving decay, the Chinese quite
simply does not feel when things need repair. This incapacity
of perceiving decay, is psychologically nothing but a
manifestation of the lack of carefulness in developing what
we have called above the sense of touch or skin.

You see how psychology helps us to obtain a real
understanding of the facts of daily life in China. Therefore
I hope that all of you will make use of the courses provided
by the psychological group and take up this study of
psychology as a means of understanding China. If Shanghai is
a progressive city, Shanghai will endeavour to get ahead of
London in applying psychology for the study of all forms of
life. The National Institute of Industrial Psychology in London

完全无法欣赏性的价值，自然意味着无法产生我们所谓的爱之不同形式的任何一种，因为所有形式的爱，包括男人之间和女人之间的友谊，都是性的升华，而所有人际关系都是从性演化而来的。所有未能将性升华的民族，都不懂得什么是爱，也没有机会利用各种形式的爱，其中许多形式作为构建人类社会的驱动力至关重要。任何所谓的中国问题专家认为，当他们指出中国人之间缺乏真正的凝聚力，缺乏合作和组织能力时，他们就发现了中国文明最严重的缺陷之一，但心理学告诉我们，这种中国人缺乏合作和组织能力的根源，在于大多数专家从未考虑过的一点。这一点就是我刚才指出的，缺乏合作和组织能力不过是无法产生普遍的人类同情心的结果，而这将是性升华的另一种形式。我今天在这里举忽视性的例子，是为了让你们理解，在中国，忽视低级感官的发展造成了多么灾难性的后果。

我在这里还要补充一点，我认为这非常重要。这种认为所有低级感官都无足轻重的中国态度，是有意且精心培养出来的，因为通过削弱低级感官，大脑切断了与所有被认为在真正的中国最为危险的刺激的联系，即来自自然的刺激。古代中国人教导说，根本的罪过是沉溺于物质，沉溺于自然；用一句话来说，就是客观性。犯下这种罪过，即死罪的危险，是被有意避免的，通过扼杀所有低级感官来避免，而这种对低级感官的扼杀成为了一种手段，使得个人不可能沉溺于任何纯粹的物理刺激之中。因此，这种扼杀低级感官的中国倾向，对于中国心理学来说，就像它对于维持中国文明的生命力和行动力具有危险性一样，是其本质所在。

我们可以补充更多事实，以证明这种忽视低级感官的中国习惯所产生的灾难性影响。在这里，皮肤被认为是不重要的，人们感觉不到污垢、灰尘或任何形式的不洁。对触觉的忽视不仅导致对清洁的忽视，还导致无法保持物品的完好维修。由于缺乏对衰败的感知，中国人根本感觉不到物品何时需要维修。这种感知衰败能力的缺失，在心理上不过是我们上面所说的触觉或皮肤感发展缺乏细致性的表现。

你们看，心理学如何帮助我们获得对中国日常生活事实的真正理解。因此，我希望你们大家都利用心理小组提供的课程，将心理学研究作为理解中国的一种手段。如果上海是一座进步的城市，上海将努力在应用心理学研究各种生命形式方面超越伦敦。伦敦的国家工业心理学研究所

page_data.en:
-11-

has up to now applied psychology only to the study of industry.
What Shanghai would need, is to apply psychology to a much
larger field of human endeavour and the China Study Center
is ready to supply this need.

In conclusion, I invite you to ask yourself how the
neglect of the lower senses in China is influencing Chinese
modernisation. Chinese modernisation is a problem which we
shall discuss in detail in our lectures introducing the
seventh, eighth and ninth group of studies of the China Study
Center, but today's lecture would be incomplete if we did
not at least briefly mention the influence which the psychological
constitution of China has upon the success of Chinese
modernisation. Therefore I invite you to imagine what is
bound to happen when the kind of psychology which I have just
described is brought into connection with modern civilization,
with electricity, steam power and all the other kinds of
mechanical power, in brief, with a world where everything is
done by machines, where machines are used by workmen who are
physically so strong that they are desirous of doing more than
their bodies can perform, and therefore avail themselves of
machines to supplement their bodily strength. In China these
machines are imposed upon a nation which has never had any
strong desire of doing anything, which has considered
quietness as an ideal, and worships Buddhas who sit with folded
legs and folded arms, closing their eyes and concentrating
themselves upon inner contemplation. With folded legs, folded
arms and closed eyes, the Chinese can live on five coppers a
day, on two bowls of rice with some vegetables, and stay in a
hut which is blown to pieces whenever there is a wind. The
Chinese is not desirous of very much change. He is a great
talker, a very weak doer. What he feels when he sees the
foreigners moving about is somewhat like this: "These foreign
devils, rushing about all day long, doing things the whole
day long, damn fools they are! foreign devils, chasing about,
depending on motor cars, big steamers, on telephones and
radiograms. Always in a hurry".

Now that is what I believe to be one of the greatest
of all human problems: this Chinese psychological constitution
which has for thousands of years been built upon the principle
of exploiting the brain, is quite simply forced out of existence
by being subjected to influences of which it understands
absolutely nothing, cannot understand anything because it was
consciously trained not to understand anything. Because
the Chinese are so very different from the foreigners, the
foreigners curse them and find them incomprehensible. Are they
so very incomprehensible? It seems to me that they are very
much like what they are bound to be if one takes their original
psychology into consideration. They are very delightful as
human beings, and thoroughly disappointing as doers of things.
They are an agricultural country which imports tremendous
amounts of its staple food, rice, every year, whose main
agricultural as well as industrial products are all decaying.
For instance, tea, silk and porcelain.

What renders Chinese modernisation so desperately
difficult is that Chinese brain-power, after having been kept
away from intercourse with the physical universe, has lost
its capacity of forming judgments concerning all questions
which are related with matters of daily life and of physical
page_data.zh:
-11-

迄今为止，心理学仅被应用于工业研究。上海所需要的是将心理学应用于更广阔的人类努力领域，而中国学社（China Study Center）已准备好满足这一需求。

最后，我请各位自问：在中国，对低级感官的忽视如何影响着中国的现代化进程。中国现代化是一个我们将在介绍中国学社第七、第八和第九组研究的讲座中详细讨论的问题，但如果我们不至少简要提及中国人的心理构成对中国现代化成功的影响，那么今天的讲座便是不完整的。因此，我请各位想象一下，当我刚才描述的那种心理学与现代文明——即电力、蒸汽动力以及所有其他形式的机械动力——相联系时，必然会发生什么；简而言之，就是在一个一切皆由机器完成的世界里，使用机器的工人在体力上如此强壮，以至于他们渴望做出超越身体极限的行为，因此利用机器来补充其体力。而在中国，这些机器被强加于一个从未有过强烈行动欲望的民族之上，该民族视宁静为理想，崇拜那些盘腿而坐、双臂交叉、闭目凝神于内省的佛像。双腿盘坐，双臂交叉，双目紧闭，中国人每天只需五个铜板，两碗米饭配些蔬菜，便能生存，栖身于风起即散的茅屋之中。中国人并不渴望太多的改变。他们是空谈家，却是极弱的行动者。当他们看到外国人四处奔忙时，心中的感受大致如下：“这些洋鬼子，整天东奔西跑，终日做事，真是该死的傻瓜！洋鬼子，到处追逐，依赖汽车、大型轮船、电话和收音机。总是匆匆忙忙。”

现在，我认为这是人类最大的问题之一：这种数千年来建立在开发大脑原则之上的中国心理构成，仅仅因为受到其完全无法理解、且因有意识地被训练成不去理解任何事物而无法理解的影响，就被简单地迫使其消亡。因为中国与外国人差异巨大，外国人咒骂他们，觉得他们不可理喻。他们真的如此不可理喻吗？在我看来，如果考虑到他们原本的心理状态，他们的表现正是必然如此。作为人，他们非常可爱；作为做事者，他们则彻底令人失望。这是一个每年进口大量主食大米的农业国家，其主要农产品及工业产品均在衰败。例如，茶叶、丝绸和瓷器。

使中国现代化变得极其困难的原因在于，中国人的脑力在长期隔绝与物理宇宙的接触后，已经丧失了就所有与日常生活及物质

page_data.en:
-12-

existence. In many cases, not only ordinary Chinese but
Chinese leaders believe that what is their poison is their
medicine. They take this poison and do not understand
why they fall ill afterwards. They show very little
capacity of judgment and still less capacity of arranging
things in their natural sequence. They very often start
at the end instead of at the beginning. They preach
progress all the time, but very seldom really know where
to begin, and when you, with the understanding of their
psychology, make a suggestion and propose to do a thing for
them, their procedure of following your advice, is very
often so unsatisfactory that the success of your undertaking
is rendered impossible. And at the end, instead of
understanding their own weakness, they will hold you
responsible for the failure. What can you do for a country
which unconsciously prevents you from doing anything even
when it believes that it has given you all possible
opportunities?

But the modernisation of China will form the subject
of at least three future lectures. Today, I believe, we
be satisfied with the success of our attempt of discussing
the problems and conditions of China in its entirety.

END OF THE FIRST LECTURE ----
page_data.zh:
-12-

生存相关的问题形成判断的能力。在许多情况下，不仅普通中国人，就连中国领导人也认为他们的毒药即是良药。他们服下这毒药，却不明白为何随后会生病。他们表现出极少的判断力，更少有能力按自然顺序安排事务。他们往往从结尾而非开头着手。他们终日宣扬进步，却很少真正知道从何开始；当你基于对其心理的理解提出建议并提议为他们做某事时，他们遵循你建议的程序往往如此令人不满，以至于你的事业成功变得不可能。最终，他们非但不理解自身的弱点，反而会将失败归咎于你。对于一个甚至在相信已给予你所有可能机会的情况下，仍无意识地阻止你做任何事情的国家，你能做什么呢？

但中国的现代化将成为至少未来三场讲座的主题。今天，我想，我们可以满足于我们尝试全面讨论中国的问题与状况所取得的成功。

第一场讲座结束 ----

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
SEPTEMBER 26, 1935

PSYCHOLOGY AND
CHINA

Over Stimulation of Brain
in North-West

Before a meeting of the psycho-
logical group of the China Study
Centre held yesterday afternoon,
Dr. Victor Frene lectured on "The
Psychological Discovery of China."
The lecture was meant as an
introduction to the work of the
psychological group of the China
Study Centre and will be followed
by other lectures providing intro-
ductions to all the other groups of
the China Study Centre. The next
lecture on Monday next October 2,
will discuss Chinese literature. The
following one will deal with Chi-
nese music. The fourth with Chi-
nese painting. All these four
lectures will supplement each other.
The lecture on "The Psychologi-
cal Discovery of China," was divid-
ed into three parts:—China's
psychological constitution, The
manifestations of the psychologi-
cal constitution of China, The ill-
effects of this constitution.
In order to render the psychologi-
cal constitution of China com-
prehensible to the foreign audience,
Dr. Frene availed himself of the
example of Goethe, who in an
advanced age developed an attitude
very similar to that of ancient
China. This attitude of Goethe is
very clearly expressed in a quota-
tion from the second part of
"Faust," which Dr. Frene quoted at
great length.
In brief, Dr. Frene wished to
explain that China in the North
West, because of the unfavourable
geographical and climatic environ-
ment was forced to rely on the
only powerful stimulation avail-
able; this stimulation was derived
from brain activity. Dr. Frene ex-
plained how this one sided depen-
dence on brain stimulation led to
the creation of Chinese literature,
music and fine arts. The speaker
discussed how the over-stimulation
of the brain led to the under
development of the lower senses
and to the consequent decay of
the power of action. This decay
of the Chinese power of action was
the fundamental defect of China
of which foreigners living in China
were generally aware. In conclu-
sion Dr. Frene endeavoured to ex-
plain how this decay of the power
of action influenced the modernisa-
tion of China.
The problem of the modernisa-
tion of China will be discussed
with great care in the lectures of
Chinese agriculture, industry and
science, which will form part of
the series of lectures to be given
by Dr. Victor Frene at the China
Study Centre.

《字林西报》
1935年9月26日

心理学与
中国

西北地区的脑部过度刺激

昨天下午，在中国学社心理学小组会议上，维克多·弗雷内（Victor Frene）博士发表了题为“中国的心理学发现”的演讲。该讲座旨在作为中国学社心理学小组工作的引言，随后还将有其他讲座，为中国学社所有其他小组提供引言。下一场讲座将于下周一（10月2日）举行，讨论中国文学。再下一场将涉及中国音乐。第四场将涉及中国绘画。这四场讲座将互为补充。
关于“中国的心理学发现”的讲座分为三个部分：一、中国的心理构成；二、中国心理构成的表现；三、这种构成的不良影响。
为了使外国听众能够理解中国的心理构成，弗雷内博士借用了歌德的例子，歌德在晚年形成了一种与古代中国非常相似的态度。歌德的这种态度在《浮士德》第二部分的引文中表达得非常清楚，弗雷内博士对此进行了长篇引用。
简而言之，弗雷内博士希望解释的是，中国西北地区由于不利的地理和气候环境，被迫依赖唯一可用的强力刺激；这种刺激源于大脑活动。弗雷内博士解释了这种对大脑刺激的片面依赖如何导致了中国文学、音乐和美术的产生。演讲者讨论了大脑的过度刺激如何导致低级感官发育不足，进而导致行动能力的衰退。这种中国人行动能力的衰退是中国的一个根本缺陷，在华外国人普遍对此有所察觉。最后，弗雷内博士试图解释这种行动能力的衰退如何影响了中国的现代化。
中国现代化的问题将在有关中国农业、工业和科学的讲座中得到仔细讨论，这些讲座将是维克多·弗雷内博士在中国学社举办的一系列讲座的一部分。

THE CHINA PRESS SATURDAY, JULY 1, 1933

Foreign Mind
Is Broadened
At Study Meet

Mental Recreation Found
At Great Western Road
Intellectual Parleys

The meeting room of the China
Study Center at 468 Great Western
Road, behind the Columbia Riding
School, is developing into a
"mental recreation center" for
foreigners, who, after a day's work,
require "mental stimulation" of a
more refined type. The lectures
on "Omnia Juncta in Uno" ("All
United in One") given by Dr.
Frere at the China Study Center
in May, have branched out into a
series of round table discussions
which provide every member of the
discussion group with an oppor-
tunity of bringing forward his
own experience and of obtaining
new solutions for his own problems.
In these discussions, which are
led by Dr. Frere, the new natural
science of psychology is, for the
first time, applied to the com-
parative study of East and West
and a new searchlight is thus
thrown upon the whole life of the
foreigner in the East. The first
discussion group, which was form-
ed in May as a result of
lectures, is still meeting every Wed-
nesday afternoon; and a second
group is being formed now for the
benefit of newcomers. This sec-
ond group is scheduled to meet
for the first time on Monday, July
3, at 5.30 p.m., at the same meet-
ing room. This second group
will again be exclusively composed
of foreigners.

On July 8, daily meetings for
Chinese in Chinese, will be in-
augurated at the China Study Cen-
ter. In these meetings the ques-
tion of regenerating China biologi-
cally, psychologically and politi-
cally, with the help of the most
modern humanized Western na-
tural science, will be discussed by
the participants. These Chinese
meetings will take place under the
auspices of Mr. Sun Fo, the son
of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and of Dr.
Tsai Yuen-pei, the famous Chinese
educationist. English and Chin-
ese prospectuses can be obtained
on application at the office of
the China Study Center, 567
Bubbling Well Road, Jessfield Apart-
ments, Flat 306, Tel. 36228.

O/C.Special Branch,
Dr.Frere advertised recently for a lady assistant
and quite a number of young & middle aged women applied. His questions
were as follows:- What kind of books do you read ? What kind of study
are you interested in ? Have you any business experience.? etc.
Two ladies know to me applied and were informed that they were too
experienced for the position. They were asked to leave their phone No.
An old woman in the employ of the Dr. stands at the door and assured
the women that the Dr. is strange at times, but that they will soon be-
come accustomed to him.

位于哥伦比亚骑马学校后方大西路468号的中国学社会议室，正逐渐发展成为外国人的“精神休憩中心”，这些外国人在一天的工作后，需要一种更精致的“精神刺激”。弗雷雷（Frere）博士五月在中国学社发表的关于“Omnia Juncta in Uno”（“万物合一”）的讲座，已衍生出一系列圆桌讨论，为讨论组的每位成员提供了提出自身经验并为自身问题寻求新解决方案的机会。在这些由弗雷雷博士主持的讨论中，心理学这门新兴自然科学首次被应用于东西方的比较研究，从而为外国人在东方的整个生活投射了一道新的探照灯。第一个讨论组是五月讲座的结果而成立的，目前仍每周三下午举行会议；现在正为新来者组建第二个小组。这第二个小组定于7月3日星期一第一次开会，时间为下午5点30分，地点仍在同一会议室。这第二个小组也将完全由外国人组成。

7月8日，中国学社将启动面向中国人的中文日常会议。在这些会议中，参与者将在最现代的人本主义西方自然科学的帮助下，讨论从生物、心理和政治层面复兴中国的问题。这些中文会议将在孙逸仙博士之子孙科先生和著名中国教育家蔡元培博士的主持下进行。中英文章程可向中国学社办公室索取，地址：静安寺路567号，杰斯菲尔德公寓306室，电话 36228。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 17, 1933

DR. VICTOR FRENE'S
CHINA LECTURES

Careful Consideration
Given To Chinese
Painting

From psychology through literature, music and painting down to the question of efficiency of manual labour and to that of the education of productive power and buying power, that was the road along which Dr. Victor Frene has guided his hearers in the course of the four lectures on Chinese problems which constituted the first series of his lectures given at the Meeting Room of the China Study Centre.

The last of the four lectures was entitled "Hill-Water Pictures." This lecture was given yesterday (Monday) afternoon. It was divided into three parts: (1) What Painting means to China. (2) The Comparative Value of Chinese Paintings. (3) Elements of the Psychology of Hill-Water Pictures. The lecture was brought to its conclusion with a discussion of the question of China's manual efficiency.

In this lecture, Dr. Frene demonstrated the fact that Chinese painting, in its essence, was not a reproduction of objects but meant to serve as what, in modern terminology, would be called a collection of ergographs, descriptive of nothing except the movement of the brain-energy of the painter himself. Therefore the only kind of Chinese paintings to be considered as fully representative of Chinese civilization were the so-called "Hill-Water Pictures" and all other types of Chinese painting were more or less fragmentary expressions of the original character of China. The art of technical drawing was more or less non-existent and even portraits were unsatisfactory. The value of colour also was never fully understood in ancient China.

Dr. Frene endeavoured to explain the causes of this defect and suggested certain fundamental remedies, the details of which will be discussed in another lecture entitled "The Education of the Buying Power of China."

维克多·弗雷内博士的
中国问题讲座

对中国绘画的
仔细考量

从心理学到文学、音乐和绘画，再到体力劳动效率的问题，以及生产力和购买力教育的问题，这就是维克多·弗雷内（Victor Frene）博士在“中国学社”（China Study Centre）会议室举行的首次系列讲座中，通过四场关于中国问题的演讲引导听众所走过的路径。

这四场讲座中的最后一场题为“山水画”。这场讲座于昨天（星期一）下午举行。它分为三个部分：(1) 绘画对中国的意义。(2) 中国绘画的比较价值。(3) 山水画的心理学要素。讲座以讨论中国体力效率的问题作为结束。

在这场讲座中，弗雷内博士论证了这样一个事实：中国绘画在本质上并非对物体的再现，而是旨在充当现代术语中所谓的“功图”（ergographs）集合，除了描述画家自身脑能量的运动外，不描述任何其他事物。因此，唯一被视为能充分代表中国文明的中国绘画类型是所谓的“山水画”，而所有其他类型的中国绘画或多或少只是中国原始性格的碎片化表达。技术绘图艺术几乎不存在，甚至肖像画也令人不满意。在古代中国，色彩的价值也从未得到充分的理解。

弗雷内博士试图解释这一缺陷的原因，并提出了一些基本的补救措施，其细节将在另一场题为“中国购买力的教育”的讲座中进行讨论。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, OCTOBER 8, 1933

A MUSICAL NOVELTY
FOR SHANGHAI

Chinese Psychology and Occidental Natural Science

To-morrow, at 5.30 p.m., Dr. Victor Frêne will give the third of his series of lectures at the meeting-room of the China Study Centre, 468 Great Western Road, speaking on "Chinese Psychology and Occidental Natural Science combined in Music." Dr. Frêne will briefly explain the psychological and scientific theories which form the background of his writings on musical psychology and Oriental music, and then, for the first time in China, will demonstrate his new method of musical interpretation, evolved out of a combination of Chinese musical Psychology with Occidental natural science. Dr. Frêne intends to form a choir for songs from the Chinese "Classic of Poetry," to demonstrate his procedure more fully, and all music-lovers are invited to make use of the first opportunity to become acquainted with the new musical conceptions, the practical application of which should provide Shanghai with a new, purely scientific, psychologically sound, and truly international form of musical self-expression.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 26, 1933

PSYCHOLOGY AND
CHINA

Over Stimulation of Brain
in North-West

Before a meeting of the psycho-
logical group of the China Study
Centre held yesterday afternoon,
Dr. Victor Frene lectured on "The
Psychological Discovery of China."
The lecture was meant as an
introduction to the work of the
psychological group of the China
Study Centre and will be followed
by other lectures providing intro-
ductions to all the other groups of
the China Study Centre. The next
lecture on Monday next October 2,
will discuss Chinese literature. The
following one will deal with Chi-
nese music. The fourth with Chi-
nese painting. All these four
lectures will supplement each other.
The lecture on "The Psychologi-
cal Discovery of China," was divid-
ed into three parts:—China's
psychological constitution, The
manifestations of the psychologi-
cal constitution of China, The ill-
effects of this constitution.
In order to render the psychologi-
cal constitution of China com-
prehensible to the foreign audience,
Dr. Frene availed himself of the
example of Goethe, who in an
advanced age developed an attitude
very similar to that of ancient
China. This attitude of Goethe is
very clearly expressed in a quota-
tion from the second part of
"Faust," which Dr. Frene quoted at
great length.
In brief, Dr. Frene wished to
explain that China in the North
West, because of the unfavourable
georgraphical and climatic environ-
ment was forced to rely on the
only powerful stimulation avail-
able; this stimulation was derived
from brain activity. Dr. Frene ex-
plained how this one sided depen-
dence on brain stimulation led to
the creation of Chinese literature,
music and fine arts. The speaker
discussed how the over-stimulation
of the brain led to the under
development of the lower senses
and to the consequent decay of
the power of action. This decay
of the Chinese power of action was
the fundamental defect of China
of which foreigners living in China
were generally aware. In conclu-
sion Dr. Frene endeavoured to ex-
plain how this decay of the power
of action influenced the modernisa-
tion of China.
The problem of the modernisa-
tion of China will be discussed
with great care in the lectures of
Chinese agriculture, industry and
science, which will form part of
the series of lectures to be given
by Dr. Victor Frene at the China
Study Centre.

《字林西报》，1933年9月26日，星期二

心理学与
中国

西北地区的脑部过度刺激

昨天下午，在中国学社心理学小组会议之前，维克多·弗雷内（Victor Frene）博士发表了题为“中国的心理学发现”的演讲。该讲座旨在作为中国学社心理学小组工作的引言，随后还将有其他讲座，为中国学社的所有其他小组提供引言。下周一（10月2日）的下一场讲座将讨论中国文学。再下一场将涉及中国音乐。第四场将涉及中国绘画。这四场讲座将相互补充。

“中国的心理学发现”这一讲座分为三个部分：—中国的心理构成，中国心理构成的表现，以及这种构成的不良影响。

为了让外国听众理解中国的心理构成，弗雷内博士利用了歌德（Goethe）的例子，歌德在晚年形成了一种与古代中国非常相似的态度。歌德的这种态度在《浮士德》第二部的一段引文中表达得非常清楚，弗雷内博士大量引用了这段话。

简而言之，弗雷内博士希望解释的是，中国西北地区由于地理和气候环境不利，被迫依赖唯一可用的强大刺激；这种刺激源于大脑活动。弗雷内博士解释了这种对大脑刺激的片面依赖如何导致了中国文学、音乐和美术的创作。演讲者讨论了大脑的过度刺激如何导致低级感官发育不良，并进而导致行动能力的衰退。这种中国人行动能力的衰退是在华外国人普遍知晓的中国根本缺陷。最后，弗雷内博士试图解释这种行动能力的衰退如何影响了中国的现代化。

中国现代化问题将在关于中国农业、工业和科学的讲座中得到仔细讨论，这些讲座将成为维克多·弗雷内博士在中国学社举办的系列讲座的一部分。

Subject (in full) The China Study Centre - Victor Westharp-Frene.

Made by D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by H.W. Robertson, Supt.

Victor Westharp-Frene, aged about 50, of heavy build,
sallow complexion, round face, slightly bald and claiming to
be a German subject, arrived in Shanghai by the S/S Sinkiang
from Canton on June 20, 1932. He brought with him some ten
cases of books.

His movements since his arrival in Shanghai have been
quite open and bear out to a great extent his claim to be here
with the intention of establishing a school, for which purpose
a house has been rented at No. 884 Yu Yuen Road.

The subject, during a conversation with the under-
signed lasting some considerable time, showed himself as
something of a fanatic. He stated that he had been in China
for 20 years during ten of which he lived as a native in
various of the northern provinces. He is undoubtedly a
Sinophil and has made a profound study of the Chinese language.

In answer to a question relative to his supposed
past connections with the universities of Canton, Westharp-
Frene stated that he had at no time been employed by any
particular establishment, but had from time to time delivered
lectures on Psychology to the more advanced students. He
made a great number of confusing references to his method of
teaching the Chinese language which would appear only to
appeal to persons with highly developed pro-Chinese tendencies,
in so far as a condition of tuition is that the student must
live and conduct himself very much as do the Chinese.

In conclusion the general information at hand
regarding the subject of this report is substantially as that
submitted by D.S. Prokofiev under report dated Sept. 9, 1932.

With reference to the advertisement published in the
"China Press" of August 11, 1937, relating to the proposed
establishment in Shanghai of a residential club for foreigners
irrespective of nationality, under the title of the "Sino Study
Centre," enquiries show that the promoter of this club is a
certain Mr. Victor Westphal-Frene who is residing in Room 510,
Cathay Hotel.

It will be recalled that this individual was the subject of
an article which appeared in the "North China Daily News" on June 8, 1937, an article
entitled "Mr. Frene, who had lived in China for nearly twenty years
and has spent the last thirteen years in the interior, calling
the same 'home', is widely regarded as the most fluent general
linguist, owing to the scientific study of China and the
Chinese, arrived in Shanghai after fifteen years in order to
become a naturalized Chinese citizen." It was also mentioned
in the same article that Mr. Frene proposed to hold a series of
lectures for foreigners and Chinese at the Association for
International Cooperation, No. 367 Route Ferguson.

Mr. Frene who is believed to be of German nationality,
is unknown to the staff of the local German Consulate-General.
He is known to have visited Shanghai on at least two occasions
during the past five years, coming from Canton. It is reported
that he is an excellent Chinese scholar, and that his attitude is
strongly pro-Chinese.

As will be seen from the attached prospectus, he
proposes to open on October 1, 1937 an establishment in the
Western district, in which people desirous of acquiring a know-
ledge of the Chinese language and Chinese culture, can reside.

ORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, JUNE 28, 1932

MR. Victor Frene, who has lived
for nearly 20 years in China and
spent more than 13 years in the
interior, applying the psychological
knowledge acquired at the Institut
General Psychologique, Paris, to the
scientific study of China and the
Chinese, has arrived in Shanghai,
after having taken steps in Nanking
to become a naturalised Chinese
citizen. Next month, he will conduct
two summer courses, one for Chinese
on the subject "Creative Reconstruc-
tion" and another, for foreigners
on "What Every Foreigner in China
Ought to Know." Details of these
courses will be announced later. Mr.
Frene's first public appearance here
will be in connection with a series
of three lectures in Chinese on June
30, July 2 and July 5 at the
Association for International Co-
operation, 383 Route Ferguson.
These lectures, which will start at
5 p.m. each day, will be devoted to
Goethe and the first will be entitled
"A Really Internationally-Minded
Man." Chinese-speaking foreigners
will be welcome to attend and ap-
plications for seats should be made
to the Association. At the end of
July, Mr. Frene will act as aesthetic
interpreter to Mr. Chen Shu-jen, the
famous painter, who is giving an
individual exhibition of his paintings.
